section: Everything start with a good research question
text:
Everything start with a good research question




1 Descriptive (What, When, Where, Who or How)
e.g. What percentageof coachees report that coaching helped them with a problem they experienced
2 Explanatory (Why?)
e.g. Why dis 65% of coachees report that coacing helped them with a problem they experienced? this





Source: Rojon, C. & Saunders, M. N. K. Formulating a convincing rationale for a research study. Coaching: An International Journal of Theory, Research and Practice 5, 55–61 (2012).

title: What is Scientific Research  for Innovation Management?
text:
Good research question: Descriptive & Explanatory
Being able to provide meaningful explanations requires answers to why (i.e. explanatory) questions in addition to what (i.e. descriptive) questions.
For example:

‘How effective is the coaching process at helping coachees to solve a problem they experience and what are the reasons for this?’
‘To what extent is the coaching process effective at helping coachees solve a problem and why?’



Source: Rojon, C. & Saunders, M. N. K. Formulating a convincing rationale for a research study. Coaching: An International Journal of Theory, Research and Practice 5, 55–61 (2012).

title: Act II: Literature review
section: Mental model when reading an abstract
text:
Mental model when reading an abstract

🌍 Topic → the writer provides background factual information.
⚠️ Problem → The writer presents the gap/problem to treat
🔎 Research Gap → the writer states the limits of current knowledge.
🎯 The purpose : the writer presents the general aim and the specific aim of the study.
📜 Methodology → the writer summarises the methodology and provides details.
📊 Results → the writer indicates the achievement of the study.
🚀 Perspectives → the writer presents the implications of the study.

title: Act II: Literature review
text:
Evidence Gaps











An evidence gap occurs with a provocative exception arises if a new research finding contradicts widely accepted conclusions.
If results from studies allow for conclusions in their own right, but are contradictory when examined from a more abstract point of view.
crumbs: CM2: On the shoulders of giants

title: Act II: Literature review
text:
Knowledge Gaps











Most common gap.
knowledge may not exist in the actual field to theories and literature from related research domains.
it might be the case that results of a study differs from what was expected
crumbs: CM2: On the shoulders of giants

title: Act II: Literature review
text:
Practical-Knowledge Gaps











Tends to be a discrepancy that can motivate new research in this direction.
A practical–knowledge (action-knowledge) conflict arises when the actual behavior of professionals is different from their advocated behavior.
Research could seek to determine the scope of the conflict and to uncover the reasons for its existence
crumbs: CM2: On the shoulders of giants

title: Act II: Literature review
text:
Methodological Gap











It deals with the conflict that occurs due to the influence of methodology on research results..
This gap addresses the conflicts with the research methods in the prior studies and offers a new line of research that is divergent from those research methods.
It might be useful to vary research methods, especially if certain research topics have been mainly explored using a singular or common method
crumbs: CM2: On the shoulders of giants

title: Act II: Literature review
text:
Empirical Gap











It deals with gaps in the prior research.
This conflict deals with the research findings or propositions need to be evaluated or empirically verified.
The empirical gap often addresses conflicts that no study to date has directly attempted to evaluate a subject or topic from an empirical approach
crumbs: CM2: On the shoulders of giants

title: Act II: Literature review
text:
Theoretical Gap











It deals with the gaps in theory with the prior research.
If one phenomenon is being explained through various theoretical models, similar to a methodological gap conflict, there might be a theoretical conflict.
Researchers and scholars could examine whether one of those theories is superior in terms of the gap in the prior research.
Theoretical gaps are a common occurrence in examining prior research on a phenomenon
crumbs: CM2: On the shoulders of giants

title: Act II: Literature review
text:
Population Gap











There are always underserved populations that have been under-researched.
The type of research regarding the population that is not adequately represented or under-researched in the evidence base or prior research (e.g., gender, race/ethnicity, age and etic)

This introduction course seeks to to Master and Engineering students to the basis of the scientific research in Innovation Management field. VOSviewer: Terminology

Maps are created by items
Items are object of interest → 📚Publications, 👩🏻‍🔬👨🏻‍🔬Researchers or 🔤Terms
Links are the relations between two items.

Each link has a Strength → Positive number. The higher, the stronger.  For instance:

Bibliographic coupling : Number of cited references two publications have in common.
Co-authorship: number of publications that two researches have co-authored.
Co-occurence: Number of publications in which two terms occur together.


Clusters are a group of items







Scientific reference


Van Eck, N.J., Waltman, L., 2010. Software survey: VOSviewer, a computer program for bibliometric mapping. Scientometrics 84, 523–538. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11192-009-0146-3
